chunks: From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Eat all things from animals except the pig, the animal that died by being gored (nathiha), the animal that died by falling (mutaraddiya), and what the wild beast ate.
If you catch any of them, and the eye is blinking or it is standing and running or its tail is twitching, then you have caught its slaughter, so eat it.
He said: 'And if you slaughtered a slaughter and you found the slaughter, and it fell into fire or into water or from above your house or a mountain, if you had found the slaughter, then eat it.'

key_terms.النَّطِيحَةُ: An animal that died by being gored (horns)
key_terms.الْمُتَرَدِّيَةُ: An animal that died by falling

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for an animal to be considered properly slaughtered and permissible to eat in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies the Shia jurisprudential principle that the validity of slaughter (dhakāh) depends on the animal being alive at the moment of the cut, rather than the specific method of death. It establishes that natural signs of life—such as a blinking eye or running—confirm the animal is fit for consumption, even if the carcass subsequently falls into fire or water, provided the slaughter was completed while it was still alive. This ruling distinguishes between animals that die from external trauma after being slaughtered and those that die from their own natural causes without the ritual cut.
